rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding statement that all in heaven and earth belong to God might suggest a finite dominion; this verse counters that inference with wonders beyond limit in His power and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك موهما لتناهي ملكه لانحصار ما في السموات وما في الأرض فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here God's words mean His wonders: wonders come about by the word Be, so the name of the cause is applied to its effect; Arabic also calls a brave opponent one's death or medicine one's cure.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالكلمة مفسرة بالعجيبة ، ووجهها أن العجائب بقوله كن وكن كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is called a word because his existence without a father was wondrous, supporting the interpretation of God's words as wonders.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى سمى المسيح كلمة لأنه كان أمرا عجيبا وصنعا غريبا لوجوده من غير أب

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that Jews claimed the Torah had mentioned everything, leaving nothing unmentioned; the verse answers that the Torah is only a drop beside God's speech.
rows.anchor: الآية واردة في اليهود حيث قالوا الله ذكر كل شيء في التوراة ولم يبق شيء لم يذكره

rows.speaker: واحد
rows.claim: Another reported occasion concerns a man who challenged the Prophet by juxtaposing the claim that human knowledge is little with the claim that wisdom is great good; the verse says it is much for people but little relative to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل أيضا إنها نزلت في واحد قال للنبي عليه السلام إنك تقول

rows.speaker: الكفار
rows.claim: A further reported occasion is a response to disbelievers who said Muhammad's teachings would run out: God's speech does not run out.
rows.anchor: وقيل أيضا إنها نزلت ردا على الكفار حيث قالوا بأن ما يورده محمد سينفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different reported occasions are disparate, showing the verse is general and can answer all of them; this general reading does not conflict with understanding the words as speech.
rows.anchor: ما ذكرتم من اختلاف الأقوال فيه يدل على جواز ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's speech is wondrous and inimitable, and belongs among His limitless wonders; the created letters and arrangement are wondrous, while the words themselves are God's attributes.
rows.anchor: كلام الله عجيب معجز لا يقدر أحد على الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse's revealed sequence differed from its written sequence, the Quran's written arrangement was commanded by God through the Messenger and is established by transmitted practice.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الآية وإن كانت نازلة على ترتيب غير الذي هو مكتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular tree with plural pens, rather than plural trees and singular pens, signals abundance: there would be pens equal in number to every tree.
rows.anchor: وحد الشجرة وجمع الأقلام ولم يقل ولو أن ما في الأرض من الأشجار أقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-baḥr is generic and encompasses every sea; the seven seas added after it are hypothetical seas beyond those that exist.
rows.anchor: تعريف البحر باللام لاستغراق الجنس وكل بحر مداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven does not limit the number: it signifies abundance, even if a thousand seas were added.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { سبعة } ليس لانحصارها في سبعة ، وإنما الإشارة إلى المدد والكثرة ولو بألف بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven became a customary number for encompassing many because space was divided into seven climes, time into seven days, and the planets were seven, to which astrologers assigned effects.
rows.anchor: هو أن ما هو معلوم عند كل أحد لحاجته إليه هو الزمان والمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ten, counting restarts at units, then hundreds build on tens and thousands on hundreds; three is the minimum complete form of beginning, middle, and end, leaving seven as the larger part of ten and a sign of abundance.
rows.anchor: أقل ما يلتئم منه أكثر المعدودات هو الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threefold counts of prayer-transition glorifications and ablution washings ease the duty by using the smaller first portion.
rows.anchor: فإن المعدودات في العبادات من التسبيحات في الانتقالات في الصلوات ثلاثة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The saying that a believer eats with one intestine and a disbeliever with seven signifies little versus much eating, not the specific number seven; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( المؤمن يأكل في معى والكافر يأكل في سبعة أمعاء ) إشارة إلى قلة الأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the same interpretation, Hell's seven gates may signal multitude; Paradise's eight gates signal its added excellence and abundance, as it contains the good and more.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال إن لجهنم سبعة أبواب بهذا التفسير

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls the conjunction before eight the wāw of eight; Razi explains it as a fresh count because customary counting completes at seven.
rows.anchor: يقول الفراء إنها واو الثمانية وليس ذلك إلا للاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No further supply is specified for the pens because the phrase already gives as many pens as existing trees, exceeding the trees; adding supplies for pens would make the sea and pens equivalent in meaning.
rows.anchor: بينا أن المراد منه هو أن يكون بعدد كل شجرة موجودة أقلام فتكون الأقلام أكثر من الأشجار الموجودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea is given additional supplies because writing consumes ink, while one pen can write many books.
rows.anchor: النقصان بالكتابة يلحق المداد أكثر فإنه هو النافد والقلم الواحد يمكن أن يكتب به كتب كثيرة

words: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's complete power and knowledge, Razi uses creation and resurrection as easy as that of one soul to answer people who find the gathering difficult: God tells the dead Be and they are.
rows.anchor: لما بين كمال قدرته وعلمه ذكر ما يبطل استبعادهم للمعشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what they say and sees what they do; His ability to resurrect and awareness of speech and deeds require complete restraint and caution.
rows.anchor: سميع لما يقولون بصير بما يعملون فإذا كونه قادرا على البعث ومحيطا بالأقوال والأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means whether they will be in or enter a new creation; their rejection is not limited to recreating them, since they deny all the afterlife, including punishment and reward.
rows.anchor: أي أئنا كائنون في خلق جديد أو واقعون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they deny resurrection because of their unbelief: they reject it because they reject what follows from it; Razi then turns to their course from death to punishment.
rows.anchor: أو نقول معناه لم ينكروا البعث لنفسه بل لكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse begins to describe what awaits them from death through punishment, following the account of their denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثم بين ما يكون لهم من الموت إلى العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God entails that death must be followed by life.
rows.anchor: يعني لا بد من الموت ثم من الحياة بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel's being entrusted with them means he does not neglect them or delay their death when their appointed term arrives; this is his sole task.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه لا يغفل عنكم وإذا جاء أجلكم لا يؤخركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī means taking or receiving in full, and qabḍ means grasping; absolute annihilation is not a taking, so the verse indicates souls remain.
rows.anchor: فإن التوفي الاستيفاء والقبض هو الأخذ والإعدام المحض ليس بأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure souls remain with angels like a person among congenial family, increasing in clarity and strength; wicked souls are like prisoners among strangers, dwindling in strength and worsening in misery and opacity.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الروح الزكي الطاهر يبقى عند الملائكة مثل الشخص بين أهله

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The philosophers say pure souls attach to a heavenly body better than their former body and perfect themselves through it, while wicked souls gain no perfection after the second attachment.
rows.anchor: والحكماء يقولون إن الأرواح الطاهرة تتعلق بجسم سماوي خير من بدنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi agrees with the philosophers if this is what they mean; otherwise their account may be true or false depending on their intended meaning.
rows.anchor: فإن أرادوا ما ذكر بها فقد وافقونا وإلا فيغير النظر في ذلك بحسب إرادتهم فقد يكون قولهم حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning death answers denial of revival: the angel takes the soul while bodily parts disperse, so gathering them and having the angel return what he took present no difficulty; the souls are preserved for their bodies.
rows.anchor: الملك يقبض الروح والأجزاء تتفرق فجمع الأجزاء لا بعد فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may console the Messenger because the deniers hurt him with their denial.
rows.anchor: خطابا مع الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم تشفيا لصدره فإنهم كانوا يؤذونه بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the address is general to everyone, like a conditional saying that is not intended for one particular person.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون عاما مع كل أحد كما يقول القائل إن فلانا كريم إن خدمته ولو لحظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing before their Lord intensifies their shame: a servant who wronged his lord and then stands before him feels the utmost embarrassment.
rows.anchor: لبيان شدة الخجالة لأن الرب إذا أساء إليه المربوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The participle or verb meaning they are saying is omitted; this signals extreme shame, since one overwhelmed by shame cannot speak.
rows.anchor: وحذف يقولون إشارة إلى غاية خجالتهم لأن الخجل العظيم الخجالة لا يتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they witnessed the gathering and heard the Messenger, then ask to return to worldly life to do righteous deeds; their present certainty cannot benefit them because faith and good works are accepted during earthly accountability.
rows.anchor: أبصرنا الحشر وسمعنا قول الرسول فارجعنا إلى دار الدنيا لنعمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading they claim they believe now, but ask to return because faith and righteous action only help during the period of earthly obligation; Razi says the request is false because afterlife faith and deeds are not accepted.
rows.anchor: إنا في الحال آمنا ولكن النافع الإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they deny having associated partners as in their claim that they were not polytheists, and say their fate resulted from failing to do good, not from disbelief.
rows.anchor: فقالوا إن هذا الذي جرى علينا ما جرى إلا بسبب ترك العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lower torment is worldly punishment before the afterlife: earthly punishment cannot be both extremely severe and prolonged, since severity kills and ends it, while prolonged punishment is less severe; afterlife punishment is severe and enduring.
rows.anchor: قبل عذاب الآخرة نذيقهم عذاب الدنيا فإن عذاب الدنيا لا نسبة له إلى عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly punishment has the qualities of nearness and smallness, while afterlife punishment is distant and immense; nearness best warns about worldly punishment, but greatness best warns about afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: لكن القرب في عذاب الدنيا هو الذي يصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An immediate mild punishment can deter more than a severe delayed one, just as some people prefer immediate reward to great reward later; calling worldly torment small would understate its threat, and calling the afterlife torment distant would weaken its warning.
rows.anchor: العذاب العاجل وإن كان قليلا قد يحترز منه بعض الناس أكثر مما يحترز من العذاب الشديد إذا كان آجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi gives two initial explanations for hope language about God: He makes them taste punishment as one who hopes does, gradually, or He punishes in a way that people might say will perhaps make them return.
rows.anchor: لعل هذه الترجى والله تعالى محال ذلك عليه فما الحكمة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's further account allows an act to be described as aiming hopefully at an outcome when the act itself does not make that outcome certain, even if certainty comes from outside it.
rows.anchor: كل فعل يتلوه أمر مطلوب من ذلك الفعل يصح تعليل ذلك الفعل بذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trader may hope for profit despite certainty based on outside knowledge, but one cannot say a person cuts an enemy's throat hoping he dies, since that act itself entails death; Razi distinguishes certainty grounded in the act from external certainty.
rows.anchor: فإنه يصح أن يقال يفعل كذا رجاء كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's hope that God forgive him and the command to hope for the Last Day show that hope language can apply despite certainty; torment does not itself guarantee repentance, so God's knowing the outcome does not bar genuine hope language.
rows.anchor: مع أنه كان عالما بالمغفرة لكن لما لم يكن الجزم حاصلا من نفس الفعل أطلق عليه الطمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance is to call adopted children by their fathers' names, which places things in their proper position and is more just.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ادعوهم لآبائهم } أرشد وقال : { هو أقسط عند الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqsaṭ may omit its comparison and mean more just than all speech, like the unqualified expression God is greater; alternatively, the earlier practice is understood, meaning more just than calling them sons of so-and-so.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ترك الإضافة للعموم أي أعدل كل كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their fathers are unknown, call them brothers in religion; if they are freed persons, call them the client of so-and-so.
rows.anchor: يعني قولوا لهم إخواننا وأخو فلان فإن كانوا محررين فقولوا مولى فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no blame for inadvertent forms of address such as calling someone my son out of affection or my father out of respect; these are like an unintentional oath or a slip of the tongue.
rows.anchor: فكذلك سبق اللسان في قول القائل ابني والسهو في قوله ابني من غير قصد إلى إثبات النسب سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about what hearts intend is a subject whose omitted predicate is recovered from the preceding clause: deliberate intent incurs blame.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره محذوف يدل عليه ما سبق وهو الجناح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A slip or unintentional use of son without intending to establish lineage is equivalent to a mistake, while deliberate intent incurs sin.
rows.anchor: سبق اللسان في قول القائل ابني والسهو في قوله ابني من غير قصد إلى إثبات النسب سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness is a powerful person's covering or removing a wrong by someone under his power; a servant who conceals a master's fault from fear is not thereby forgiving him.
rows.anchor: المغفرة هو أن يسترد القادر القبيح الصادر ممن تحت قدرته حتى أن العبد إذا ستر عيب سيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is kindness to someone because of their helplessness and without compensation; kindness to a powerful person, for expected benefit, or in repayment of prior kindness is not mercy in this strict sense.
rows.anchor: الرحمة هو أن يميل إليه بالإحسان لعجز المرحوم إليه لا لعوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When forgiveness precedes mercy, God first covers the wrong, then sees the servant's helplessness and gives what suffices; when forgiveness follows mercy, He first favors the helpless and then withholds punishment and covers sins.
rows.anchor: فالمغفرة إذا ذكرت قبل الرحمة يكون معناها أنه ستر عيبه ثم رآه مفلسا عاجزا فرحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the harmful consequence of women uncovering before those their right hands possess is apparent.
rows.anchor: فإن المفسدة في التكشف لهم ظاهرة

rows.speaker: بعض الأئمة
rows.claim: Some imams say the group intended by those their right hands possess is limited to people who have not reached puberty.
rows.anchor: ومن الأئمة من قال المراد من كان دون البلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God indicates that uncovering before enslaved people is conditional on safety and knowledge that no harm will result.
rows.anchor: عند المماليك دليل على أن التكشف لهم مشروط بشرط السلامة والعلم بعدم المحذور

words: إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's witnessing is especially apt after the permissions for seclusion and uncovering: He witnesses private encounters as fully as public ones, so they should fear Him.
rows.anchor: فخلوتكم مثل ملئكم بشهادة الله تعالى فاتقوا

words: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After respect rules for the Prophet's private household, this verse completes the account of his honor in public: he is honored in the highest assembly by God and the angels, and in the lower assembly believers must honor him.
rows.anchor: لما أمر الله المؤمنين بالاستئذان وعدم النظر إلى وجوه نسائه احتراما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalāt means prayer or supplication in Arabic, but that sense cannot apply to God because supplication asks a third party to benefit someone; al-Shāfiʿī says the word is used with distinct meanings.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى غير معقول في حق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 33:43 God is named separately before the angels, while here God and angels share a plural predicate; naming one before a conjunct signals precedence, like saying the king enters and another, and exalts the Prophet as the focal recipient of prayer.
rows.anchor: كما أن الملك إذا قال يدخل فلان وفلان أيضا يفهم منه تقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Prophet, God's prayer is foundational and the angels join it as something incumbent or recommended whether or not God has prayed; for believers, the angels' prayer does not have that same status.
rows.anchor: فقال في حق النبي عليه السلام إنهم يصلون إشارة إلى أنه في الصلاة على النبي عليه السلام كالأصل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Because the command entails obligation, al-Shāfiʿī takes this verse to require prayer upon the Prophet in the tashahhud; Razi says it is not obligatory outside it.
rows.anchor: هذا دليل على مذهب الشافعي لأن الأمر للوجوب فتجب الصلاة على النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When asked how to pray upon him, the Prophet taught the formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family, and to grant them blessing as He did them; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: النبي عليه السلام كيف نصلي عليك يا رسول الله ؟ فقال : ( قولوا اللهم صل على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers' prayers do not meet a need of the Prophet, just as he needs no angelic prayer; they express reverence and, out of mercy for believers, earn them reward.
rows.anchor: كما أن الله تعالى أوجب علينا ذكر نفسه ولا حاجة له إليه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said that whoever prays upon him once receives ten prayers from God; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: من صلى علي مرة صلى الله عليه عشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not left under the community's favor for praying for him, since God directs him to pray for the community, whose comfort is in his prayers.
rows.anchor: لم يترك الله النبي عليه السلام تحت منة أمته بالصلاة حتى عوضهم منه بأمره بالصلاة على الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to salute is obligatory, and because it is not required outside prayer, the salutation Peace be upon you, O Prophet is required in tashahhud; this opposes those who deny its obligation.
rows.anchor: أمر فيجب ولم يجب في غير الصلاة فيجب فيها وهو قولنا السلام عليك أيها النبي في التشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun emphasizes completing the salutation; the prayer is not reinforced with the same emphasis because the preceding clause already confirms it.
rows.anchor: ولم يؤكد الصلاة بهذا التأكيد لأنها كانت مؤكدة

words: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many ordinary people worship God chiefly to avert harm or obtain benefit. The preceding verse says none but God can avert harm, and this verse says provision and benefit also come only from Him; the elect worship for His greatness regardless.
rows.anchor: أن العامة يعبدون الله لا لكونه إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the interlocutors do not answer, the Prophet should say that God provides; people acknowledge God as remover of harm in distress but remain heedless of Him in ease.
rows.anchor: عند الضر ذكر أنهم يقولون الله ويعترفون بالحق

words: وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو فى ضلال مبين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches a calm method of debate: direct accusations anger opponents and impair reasoning, while admitting that one side is mistaken invites joint examination, avoids stubbornness, and does not lower the Prophet's standing despite his certainty that he is guided.
rows.anchor: هذا إرشاد من الله لرسوله إلى المناظرات الجارية في العلوم وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance takes ʿalā because the guided person is metaphorically elevated and looking out, while error takes fī because the errant person is submerged in darkness.
rows.anchor: في الهدى كلمة على وفي الضلال كلمة في لأن المهتدي كأنه مرتفع متطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Error is described as manifest but guidance is not: the straight path to truth is unique, whereas error includes many degrees, some clearer than others.
rows.anchor: الهدي هو الصراط المستقيم الموصل إلى الحق والضلال خلافه لكن المستقيم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance precedes error because it describes the believers identified by we, and they are mentioned first.
rows.anchor: قدم الهدى على الضلال لأنه كان وصف المؤمنين المذكورين بقوله
